items.stem: In the Microsoft-recommended rollout, what are the three phases in order?

options.rationale: Correct: the phases are pilot, deploy, then operate.
Operate follows deployment, not precedes the pilot.
This is not the documented phased approach.

items.stem: Which TWO help drive Copilot adoption? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A champions programme of engaged early adopters
options.rationale: Correct: champions help peers adopt and contextualise value.

options.text: Using the usage report to identify and nudge inactive users
options.rationale: Correct: the usage report surfaces inactive users to re-engage.

options.text: Measuring only how many licences were assigned
options.rationale: Licences assigned does not equal active, valuable usage.

options.text: Hiding usage data from business leaders
options.rationale: Sharing adoption insight with leaders supports the programme.

items.explanation: Correct: champions help peers adopt and contextualise value.

items.stem: Why complete a readiness assessment and get data ready before broad deployment?

options.text: Because Copilot surfaces content based on existing permissions, so oversharing must be addressed first
options.rationale: Correct: readiness includes governing data so Copilot does not amplify oversharing.

options.text: Because Copilot requires every file to be deleted first
Because readiness assessment assigns the licences
options.rationale: Readiness is separate from licence assignment.

options.text: Because deployment is impossible without it
options.rationale: It is strongly recommended, not a hard technical blocker.

items.explanation: Correct: readiness includes governing data so Copilot does not amplify oversharing.
